extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials and managers responsible for scientific, technical, and engineering information (STI) implementation of OMB Circular A-130
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and recommendations for federal agencies on managing scientific, technical, and engineering information (STI) under OMB Circular A-130, including planning, dissemination, integrity, records/archival issues, and international exchange. Focuses on improving usability, quality, and interagency coordination of STI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance planning for numeric data programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality assurance planning is a key element in improving collection efforts in numeric data programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA’s EMAP program emphasizes the ISO 9000 standard as well as other quality assurance tools and techniques. Agencies should provide guidance to programs contributing data so that they can structure their approach to data collection and integration to be more cost-effective, less burdensome, and higher quality. (Examples: EPA, NAL/AGRICOLA; emphasis on standardization of exchange formats and upgrading collection/transmission technology.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Information life-cycle planning
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular Section 8.a.(1) calls for integrated life-cycle planning for information and outlines objectives for that planning process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Life-cycle planning should be clarified to address planning for the use of information in terms of its value for research and development, decisionmaking, and ensuring an adequate record of STI activities. STI often lacks a single 'cradle-to-grave' life cycle; planning must account for permanent or long-term value, retention and use, and the fact that value may not be determinable at creation. Agencies should receive additional guidance so information content planning and information systems planning differences are clear; OMB should develop guidelines and a model system addressing integration of content and systems planning. (Recommendation: Clarify 'life-cycle planning' for information usability.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate emphasis on information content as well as information systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Information management guidance should give at least an equal emphasis to information content as to information systems to ensure usability issues are sufficiently addressed by agency planners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRM processes historically focus on technology acquisition rather than information utilization; data calls and IRM reviews often emphasize technology, producing burdensome responses that underrepresent content issues. Planning guidance should include specific information dissemination objectives, encourage cooperation of dissemination activities within agencies, and re-evaluate the traditional IRM function under Reinventing Government to ensure content objectives are not neglected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify scope of public access and dissemination responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: 0MB’s intent in the Circular regarding the extent to which agencies are to provide access to STI to all citizens should be clarified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Circular does not clearly define whether 'announcement' of the existence of information is sufficient for compliance or whether agencies must actively promote and deliver full text. Agencies should be told how far outreach/public promotion must go so they can allocate scarce resources effectively. Planning for dissemination should include STI managers and better coordination within and between agencies to avoid inefficient or duplicative outreach efforts. Models would be useful to help balance mission resources versus non-mission public-access activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information integrity and authenticity controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of the nature of STI, the public good may be better served with controls over some types of information than with unrestricted reuse — particularly where government data integrity and authenticity must be maintained to protect public health, welfare, or national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should not be prohibited exclusively from exerting some control over organizations that seek to redistribute Federal STI. Guidelines should be developed enabling agencies to require redisseminators — regardless of trademark use — to comply with appropriate procedures that ensure data integrity and authenticity (accuracy, completeness, currency, and timely correction of errors). NLM licensing arrangements (requiring licensees to correct errors and update products) are cited as examples that prevented harm (case histories of dosage errors, retractions, MeSH corrections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Require and provide adequate metadata and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuse and downloading of data without necessary metadata is a special concern; metadata allow users to know the accuracy of data and to judge their validity for intended uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metadata should include not only technical specifications (record layouts, data element definitions) but also information that enables users to assess accuracy, completeness, currency, and suitability for particular uses. Agencies should ensure metadata accompany STI to prevent misuse and misinterpretation of data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usability and accessibility of electronic dissemination systems
rubrics_metrics.description: As electronic dissemination systems are developed there should be a focus on making these systems more usable for the customer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: User-friendly (particularly graphical) interfaces are a high priority. Systems should accommodate low-end as well as high-end user environments and provide document delivery in a variety of formats (electronic and paper). Emphasize directories and networking using transparent protocols to help users navigate; include extensive user help features (examples: DTIC GoldenGate, DTIC Mosaic use, NOAA SAA improvements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Records management and archival models for electronic STI
rubrics_metrics.description: STI does not have the same 'cradle-to-grave' life cycle as information systems; models for records management in the new electronic paradigm do not yet exist but are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer of electronic copies to NARA for archival purposes can occur without removing information from the originating agency; retention decisions will depend on anticipated demand and system capacity. Evaluating long-term value of scientific records requires specialized expertise (NARA contracted NRC for advice). Agencies need models and policies for conversion, preservation, and disposition of legacy records, recognizing that conversion/preservation can be costly and sensitive (health/environment data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance A-130 restrictions with national and international STI exchange requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular A-130's prohibition on agencies establishing exclusive or restricted distribution arrangements can weaken agencies' ability to operate cooperative international exchange, partnerships, and technology transfer activities that require honoring redistribution restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must be able to honor restrictions requested by foreign exchange partners and pass those restrictions on when necessary; in some cases the value of international information justifies accepting redistribution conditions. The Circular should be clarified or adjusted so agencies (e.g., NASA) are not prevented from protecting international partner data and thereby jeopardizing exchange relationships critical to national interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish policy for STI advocacy and coordinated management within agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure that agencies’ STI is managed in a coherent, coordinated manner, OMB should establish policy for the advocacy of STI within Federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB action is suggested to create policy that elevates STI concerns within agencies, facilitating cooperation among program offices and information dissemination units, and ensuring senior management support for STI activities that often are viewed as overhead rather than mission-essential functions.
